title: Geometric perspective on quantum Rabi model: Super adiabatic universality and curvature non-adiabatic effects
abstract: Quantum Rabi model (QRM) is a fundamental model in light-matter interactions (LMIs), whereas this finite-component system manifests infinite physics to be explored and a full understanding has not yet been reached after a hundred years since it was proposed. In the present work we create a geometric perspective for the QRM by mapping to a curved nanowire system, with curvature-induced spin-orbit coupling (SOC) manipulatable by LMI strength and frequency ratio, which is capable of revealing and perceiving the property universality and diversity from the ground state to the whole spectrum in a unified picture. Indeed, we unveil a super university in the adiabatic regime which manifests a universal scaling of spin texture ubiquitously valid for different couplings, different frequencies and different energy levels. The curve frame also facilitates our finding that a direction changeover of tangential spin swing emerges in the non-adiabatic spin texture in association with the quantum phase transition (QPT) in the QRM, which endows a geometric non-adiabaticity interpretation and connotation to the QPT. We also clarify that, among the curvature-induced effects, the SOC accounts for the spectral bifurcation and oscillations. Our method and analysis, readily generalized to other light-matter models, opens a dialogue between geometry and physics, thus paving a novel way to gain deeper insight into LMIs.
summary: This paper introduces a novel geometric framework by mapping the Quantum Rabi Model (QRM) onto a curved nanowire system. This approach allows the authors to reveal a 'super-universality' in the adiabatic regime and provides a geometric interpretation for the QRM's quantum phase transition. The method offers a powerful tool for gaining deeper insights into light-matter interactions.
main_problem: To develop a unified, geometric perspective for the Quantum Rabi Model (QRM) to understand its universal properties and the nature of its quantum phase transitions (QPTs).
main_result: The geometric mapping reveals a 'super-universality' in the adiabatic regime and provides a geometric interpretation for the QPT via a changeover in the non-adiabatic spin texture.
method: The authors map the QRM to a curved nanowire system, employing geometric analysis, local diagonalization, and semiclassical approximations to analyze the system's behavior.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the Quantum Rabi Model (QRM), a fundamental model for light-matter interactions (LMIs). The analysis involves mapping this system onto a curved nanowire Hamiltonian that incorporates curvature-induced spin-orbit coupling (SOC).
key_observables: Super-universality of spin texture, changeover of tangential spin swing direction, spectral bifurcation, and spectral oscillations.
important_parameters: LMI strength ($g$), frequency ratio ($\omega/\Omega$), and the curvature of the nanowire geometry.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the system to a curved geometry and utilizing approximations like the semiclassical limit in certain regimes.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares adiabatic basis results with exact diagonalization for QPT analysis. Figure 2 illustrates the mapping of the QRM onto a curved nanowire system, showing paths dependent on coupling and frequency.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the QRM, develops the geometric mapping to a curved nanowire, analyzes the adiabatic and non-adiabatic regimes to find universal scaling laws, and interprets the QPT through geometric non-adiabaticity.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges geometry (curved manifolds) with fundamental quantum physics (light-matter interaction), offering a powerful, generalizable framework for understanding complex quantum dynamics beyond simple approximations.
